balance.notaExportador.message: On 28-A Spain was a net exporter to France and Portugal with 870 + 2,600 MW, emptying its own reserves while the system oscillated. Negative values = import.

waterfall.item1.fuente.message: CEER 2023 (VoLL) + ERSE/REN (PT ENS) + ES ENS estimate

waterfall.item1.nota.message: ES ENS is an estimate — open question (see datos28A.json)

waterfall.footerText1.message: VoLL Methodology: The cost of energy not supplied is calculated at 11,000 €/MWh (weighted residential/industrial average for Spain, CEER 2023, Appendix B), based on an estimated ENS of ~255,490 MWh (55,489 MWh verified in Portugal — ERSE/REN; ~200,000 MWh estimated for Spain — data not verified in primary source).

waterfall.footerText2.message: Reinforced Operation (666 M€): verified data in primary source (REE, April 2026 report).

waterfall.footerFallback.message: ⚠ This analysis includes estimates not verified in a primary source. See datos28A.json § reposicion.ens_espana_total for the open question declaration. Estimated total: {total} M€.

thermal.fallbackBanner.message: ⚠ REData API unavailable — estimated data (deterministic fallback). Hourly values are estimates consistent with verified ranges, not direct measurements from ESIOS. See methodological note.

thermal.heatmapAria.message: Heatmap of electrical adjustment services costs during the week of 28-A. The peak of costs is concentrated on April 28, 2025 between 12:00 and 15:00 CEST.

thermal.footerText.message: Verified costs (ISE-2025 REE / REE April 2026 report): The total cost of adjustment services in 2025 increased by +43% compared to 2024, with technical constraints accumulating between 3,351 and 3,770 M€ due to the forced dispatch of combined cycles ("Reinforced Operation"). The cumulative cost of the Reinforced Operation until March 31, 2026 was 666 M€ (REE, April 2026 report — verified data). In March 2026, constraints represented 28% of the energy term in the PVPC bill.

thermal.footerFallback.message: ⚠ Hourly data: deterministic estimates consistent with ISE-2025 REE ranges. They do not come from direct ESIOS measurements — individual values are an OPEN QUESTION.

thermal.footerSource.message: Source: ESIOS / REE (Indicators 680, 71-74, 638) · Period: Apr 26 – May 02, 2025.

pvcurve.marginCollapse.message: 💥 VOLTAGE COLLAPSE — System without stable solution

pvcurve.scrHintWeak.message: ⚠ Weak grid — high voltage vulnerability (28-A condition)

pvcurve.footer.message:
Voltage collapse mechanism (P-V nose curve): The stable branch (blue) represents the normal operation of the system. The nose point (red dot) is the maximum loadability: beyond this, there is no stable solution for the reactive power flow equation. On 28-A, the peninsular south zone operated with SCR ≈ 1.8 and a load equivalent to 91% of the maximum capacity of the reactive corridor, leaving a negative margin before the first trip.
Model: 2-node system (Van Cutsem & Vournas, 1998). Parameters anchored to ENTSO-E Factual Report, Table 2-4, p. 36.

eas.evt1.label.message: Stable. Start of controlled sub-synchronous local oscillations.

eas.evt1.evidence.message: 400 kV voltages below the admissible limits of 420 kV.

eas.evt2.label.message: Physical tripping of interconnections due to loss of synchronism.

eas.evt3.label.message: Abrupt transition. Absolute omission of Alert and Emergency states.

eas.evt3.evidence.message: Collapse. Disconnection of 2,500 MW of generation and Pyrenean interconnections.

eas.evt4.label.message: Instantaneous fall of the Portuguese synchronous block.

eas.evt5.label.message: Activation of the frequency control protocol in split mode.

eas.evt5.evidence.message: Operating in synchronous split mode relative to Iberia.

eas.evt6.label.message: Security coordination of the continental synchronous block.

eas.evt7.label.message: Physical disconnection of interconnections and safe isolation of the French system.

eas.evt7.evidence.message: Transient voltage fluctuations mitigated in border substations.

eas.evt8.label.message: Normalization of voltages in southern France.

eas.evt9.label.message: Start of the physical restoration plan of the Portuguese system.

eas.evt9.evidence.message: Construction of local bottom-up islands with black-start units.

eas.evt10.label.message: Report of REE LFC operability. Exchange ramp from 0 to 1,400 MW.

eas.evt11.label.message: Loop closure and stabilization of REE AGC.

eas.evt11.evidence.message: The Spanish system recovers automatic control and deviation compensation.

CostOfInactionChart.title.message: The cost of inaction: resilience CAPEX vs VoLL exposure (2025–2030)

CostOfInactionChart.subtitle.message: Comparison between accumulated investment in resilience infrastructure and the expected economic exposure if the current low-grid-strength architecture is maintained. When the VoLL curve exceeds the CAPEX curve, inaction is more expensive than investment. Values beyond 2026 are projections. Select a deployment scenario.

CostOfInactionChart.scenarioLabel.description: Label for scenario selector in CostOfInactionChart

CostOfInactionChart.crossingLabel.description: Label shown at the CAPEX/VoLL crossing point

CostOfInactionChart.reading.base.message: CAPEX disbursement following the PERTE ERHA schedule. The indifference point between investing and not investing falls in 2027: from that year, cumulative VoLL exposure exceeds total committed CAPEX. The Operational Reinforcement would cost over 6,600 M€ accumulated by 2030.
CostOfInactionChart.reading.base.description: Reading card text for base scenario

CostOfInactionChart.reading.acelerado.message: If CAPEX is brought forward one year through fiscal incentives, the cumulative VoLL exposure never exceeds the cost of investment within the 2030 horizon. The effective payback period falls to 2.4 years.
CostOfInactionChart.reading.acelerado.description: Reading card text for accelerated scenario

CostOfInactionChart.reading.retrasado.message: Regulatory paralysis deferring CAPEX to 2027 causes projected VoLL exposure to exceed 8,000 M€ by 2030 — more than double the required CAPEX. Each year of delay adds approximately 820 M€ in structural overrun.
CostOfInactionChart.reading.retrasado.description: Reading card text for delayed scenario

CostOfInactionChart.methodNote.message: ⚠ Values beyond 2026 are projections. CAPEX: 3,010 M€ BESS+SynCons + 650 M€ P.O.7.4 retrofit (Engie-Rolwind; CNMC). Projected OR: 1,200 M€/year on real REE data (666 M€ to Mar-2026). VoLL: ACER/CEER methodology, probability of systemic event × expected ENS under weak architecture (ERAA post-28A).

ReserveMarginDegradationFigure.title.message: IBR penetration and escalation of adjustment costs (2020–2025)

ReserveMarginDegradationFigure.subtitle.message: As asynchronous generation displaced synchronous mass from the mix, technical restriction and adjustment service costs escalated non-linearly. The 2025 Operational Reinforcement is the visible consequence of this structural accumulation. Click each year to expand.

ReserveMarginDegradationFigure.annotOR.description: Annotation label for OR year in chart

ReserveMarginDegradationFigure.methodNot.message: ⚠ IBR penetration: fraction of peninsular generation provided by technologies without direct synchronous coupling (PV, full-converter wind, inverter-based storage). Restriction and adjustment service costs: REE/ESIOS published settlements. The 2025 figure includes the Operational Reinforcement surcharge (May–Dec 2025; REE official note Apr 2026).
